A control search that kept exactly half of the aircraft time (frac = 0.5) is treated as degenerate and ignored by the rules. The documented definition says a control is degenerate only when it keeps LESS than half. Expected: frac = 0.5 counts as a real control.

from jf import rules


def test_half_aircraft_time_is_a_real_control():
    control = {"kind": "flip", "best": 10.0, "verdict": "nothing", "frac": 0.5}
    assert not rules.is_degenerate(control)

    out = rules.evaluate([(100.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)], [control], 5.0, [])
    assert out["nulls_used"] == 1
    assert out["nulls_degenerate"] == 0
    assert out["null_best"] == 10.0
    assert all(out["conditions"][key] for key in ("a", "a_flip", "b", "c", "d"))
    assert out["v32"] == "one"


def test_fraction_strictly_below_threshold_is_degenerate():
    assert rules.is_degenerate({"frac": 0.499})
    assert not rules.is_degenerate({"frac": 0.501})
    assert not rules.is_degenerate({"frac": 0.7}, degenerate_frac=0.7)
    assert rules.is_degenerate({"frac": 0.699}, degenerate_frac=0.7)
